1.explanation: In the ComboBox’s internal render logic, each <ListBox.MenuItem> is assigned a React key of `item.id != null ? item.id : itemToString(item)`. When your data objects don’t have an `id` field, it falls back to `itemToString(item)`. If you have two items whose stringified value is the same (both return “Option”), React logs a warning because you’ve provided duplicate keys. This minimal example omits any `id` fields on the items, and both items have the same text, reproducing the duplicate-key warning.
1.bug_scenario: The ComboBox is rendering two menu items whose labels are identical (“Option”), and because neither item has a unique `id`, the code falls back to using `itemToString(item)` as the React `key`. Both menu items end up with the same key, triggering the React warning about duplicate keys.
